exposure: onset of SIPE (early-onset before 34 weeks gestation vs late-onset at or after 34 weeks gestation)
outcome: Hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, low platelet count (HELLP) syndrome
cohort: 311 pregnant individuals with superimposed preeclampsia who delivered at 22 weeks' gestation or greater at an academic institution
finding: Individuals with early-onset superimposed preeclampsia had higher odds of adverse maternal outcomes, including a composite of eclampsia, HELLP syndrome, maternal death, placental abruption, pulmonary edema, superimposed preeclampsia with severe features, and thromboembolic disease, compared to those with late-onset superimposed preeclampsia.
mod_finding: This study found that women with early-onset superimposed preeclampsia had higher odds of cesarean delivery compared to those with late-onset superimposed preeclampsia.
